Competitor News.title: At Barclays Center, a new look emerges with art, clubs and the cloud
Competitor News.summary: At Barclays Center, a new look emerges with art, clubs and the cloud NetsDaily
Competitor News.copy:
Barclays Center looked different when Brooklyn Nets fans arrived for Opening Night Wednesday, their first game since look on April 9. On one level, it’s part of yet another upgrade at the arena but on another level, it’s different. It’s not just brick-and-mortar improvement at entrances, better ingress and egress or a new club (or two.) It’s about art and cloud technology and an immersive in-house experience to pull fans away from the comfort of their own home and into the Nets own space.

Some of it is temporary, some is permanent but all of it was quite visible … and visual. The most noteworthy addition is temporary, but will make appearances throughout the season, but it certainly qualifies as art. The Nets 60th anniversary court, dressed up in ABA colors, was striking and it included a feature that blew a lot of minds. Around the edges of the court were the names of all 575 players who ever donned one of the Nets many uniforms going back to the New Jersey Americans. There was Brook Lopez who holds the career record for points as well as Wenyen Gabriel who played one game as a COVID replacement.

Contemporary art is the portal through which many people start collecting: One of the most exciting, dynamic, and accessible parts of the market, it is a vital gateway for new buyers.

Wider Sports News.title: Allianz secures naming rights to LA28 venue
Wider Sports News.summary: Allianz secures naming rights to LA28 venue Sports Business Journal
bullets: Allianz has secured the naming rights to an LA28 venue in Long Beach, which will be known as Allianz Beach Arena. It will host beach volleyball during the Olympics and blind soccer during the Paralympics. The nearly 15,000-seat temporary venue will be built on the Long Beach waterfront and is expected to host more than 700,000 spectators. Financial terms were not disclosed.

LA28 is the first organising committee able to sell venue naming rights, under a pilot programme approved by the International Olympic Committee. The Comcast Squash Center at Universal Studios is the only other temporary venue sold so far, while Honda Center and Intuit Dome keep their names during the Games. Chairman Casey Wasserman previously put the price at nine figures. Allianz, a global sponsor since 2021, holds naming rights to seven venues worldwide and will launch a custom LA28 logo featuring Allianz Arena and Allianz Field.
Wider Sports News.copy:
Allianz has secured the naming rights to one of LA28’s venues in Long Beach, marking one of the first sponsors to put its name on one of the Games’ temporary venues. bullets: Academics at the University of Stirling, Dr Richard Purves and Dr Catherine Best, have called on the Scottish Government to consider comprehensive restrictions on alcohol sports sponsorship. Alcohol branding was more prevalent during the matches themselves than in commercial breaks.

SHAAP chair Dr Alastair MacGilchrist said viewers saw alcohol branding around every two minutes, and that self-regulation has not protected children and young people. He urged the government to set out restrictions and a timetable in its alcohol harm prevention plan, due this year. He cited France, which has banned alcohol sports sponsorship for more than 30 years, and noted that most Scottish Premiership clubs have alcohol-industry sponsors or partnerships.

Wider Sports News.summary: JJ Lin, Tia Ray & Lil Ghost Take the Formula 1 Singapore Grand Prix Stage With Support From TME Financial Times
bullets: Singers JJ Lin, Tia Ray and Lil Ghost performed at the Formula 1 Singapore Grand Prix on 9 October 2026 as part of Tencent Music Entertainment Group (TME)'s efforts to bring Chinese-language artists to international stages. Tia Ray performed tracks including "Love Herby" and "Beautiful Day", while Lil Ghost gave the live world premiere of "Wild Card" from his album "KUI". JJ Lin closed the night on the main stage with a 20-song show involving a 100-member international team, after nearly six months of preparation, and debuted his English-language single "RISE WITHOUT A SOUND".

The performances drew a positive response from the artists and fans, and the sets of Tia Ray and Lil Ghost generated attention on Chinese social media, with many fans saying they intended to travel to Singapore the following year. JJ Lin, a long-time Formula 1 enthusiast, described the appearance in his home country as a dream stage. TME said it will deepen its partnerships with the Formula 1 Singapore Grand Prix and other global collaborators, creating more opportunities for Chinese-language artists to reach international audiences.
Wider Sports News.copy:
, Oct. 20, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- JJ Lin, Tia Ray and Lil Ghost brought their distinctive sounds to the Formula 1 Singapore Grand Prix on October 9, 2026, energizing the evening's entertainment in Singapore with performances that brought music and motorsport together for a global audience. The appearances were part of Tencent Music Entertainment Group (TME)'s efforts to bring leading artists from the Chinese-language music scene to international stages.

Chinese R&B diva and acclaimed singer-songwriter Tia Ray performed signature tracks including "Love Herby" and "Beautiful Day", blending Eastern influences with international musical elements to highlight the distinctive sound and global outlook of Chinese R&B. She had recently headlined a solo show at the Grammy Museum, making her the first Chinese female singer to do so. Visionary singer-songwriter Lil Ghost performed material from his new album "KUI", staging the world live premiere of his track "Wild Card", backed by a full-band lineup and performing songs including "Saturday Night". His commanding stage presence energized the crowd. Together, the two artists showcased contemporary Chinese-language music through their distinct styles, drawing interest from music fans and motorsport enthusiasts around the world.

Rugby.title: Ireland prop Furlong cited over alleged groin grab
Rugby.summary: Ireland prop Tadhg Furlong is cited over an alleged groin grab in Leinster's United Rugby Championship win over Munster on Saturday.
bullets: Ireland prop Tadhg Furlong has been cited over an alleged groin grab during Leinster's 24-18 United Rugby Championship win over Munster at the Aviva Stadium on Saturday. Munster back row Gavin Coombes raised the allegation with referee Andrew Brace in the 37th minute, but television match official Colin Stanley found no video evidence at the time. Furlong has been cited under Law 9.27, and the URC said disciplinary arrangements would be announced in due course.

If found guilty, the 33-year-old could miss Ireland's Nations Championship matches against Argentina, Fiji and South Africa in Dublin, plus the finals weekend in London. South Africa's Jan-Hendrik Wessels received a nine-match suspension in October 2025 for a similar offence, after a 12-week ban was reduced by three weeks. A comparable sanction would also rule Furlong out of Leinster's Champions Cup pool match with Sale and the festive derbies with Ulster and Munster.
Rugby.copy:
Ireland prop Tadhg Furlong has been cited over an alleged groin grab in Leinster's United Rugby Championship win over Munster on Saturday. Munster back row Gavin Coombes raised the allegation against an unnamed Leinster player with match referee Andrew Brace in the closing stages of the first half at the Aviva Stadium, but television match official (TMO) Colin Stanley could not find any video evidence at the time.

However, experienced front row Furlong has now been cited over an act of foul play under Law 9.27, which says a "a player must not do anything that is against the spirit of good sportsmanship including but not limited to grabbing, twisting or squeezing the genitals".

George Ford would come into contention to deputise if Smith is ruled out, and Marcus Smith is the third fly-half in the elite squad, though Borthwick sees him primarily as a full-back. They host Australia at Allianz Stadium, Twickenham on Sunday 8 November in Round 4 of the Nations Championship, before facing Japan and New Zealand.

Rugby.summary: World Rugby confirms law change – but it’s too late for injured international Ruck.co.uk
bullets: Dragons head coach Filo Tiatia has urged World Rugby to bring forward its new tackle law after a knee-drop tackle forced Tongan international Fetuli Paea off injured in the Dragons' 31-14 defeat to the Ospreys at St Helen's. Tiatia called the tackle dangerous and said Paea's condition would be assessed medically.

World Rugby confirmed a few weeks ago that knee-drop tackles will be outlawed from 1 November. The change forms part of a wider effort to reduce dangerous contact, and World Rugby has also confirmed that the hip-drop tackle is to be removed. Tiatia, a former New Zealand international, pointed to the NRL's strict approach to the technique, while the tackle on the 32-year-old Paea remains permitted under the current laws.
Rugby.copy:

World Rugby confirmed only a number of weeks ago that knee-drop tackles will be outlawed by November 1, but Tiatia believes they should not wait until then to act. Paea was forced off injured in the Gwent side’s 31-14 defeat at the newly revamped St Helen’s, as Tiatia made his feelings clear following the full-time whistle.

However, he became available to Borthwick again having returned to England to play for Sale Sharks and is part of a training squad which assembled on Sunday for a three-day camp.

bullets: Munster head coach Clayton McMillan has backed number eight Gavin Coombes, who alleged he was grabbed in the groin by an unnamed Leinster player at a ruck late in the first half of Saturday's 24-18 United Rugby Championship defeat at the Aviva Stadium. Coombes raised the matter with referee Andrew Brace, but TMO Colin Stanley found no video evidence of the incident.

McMillan said he backs his players "100%" when they make such allegations and that it was now for "the powers that be", referring to the citing commissioner, who can review incidents retrospectively. Leinster head coach Leo Cullen said he did not see the incident and called it a "serious matter" for the citing commissioner. He added that Coombes appeared to change his mind midway through the accusation, and that he could see nothing himself.
Rugby.copy:

Coombes raised the allegation with match referee Andrew Brace, but the television match official (TMO), Colin Stanley, could not find any video evidence of the incident. bullets: Wales beat Japan in Tokyo to secure a second victory of their WXV campaign, in swirling wind, rain and humidity between the sides ranked 11th and 12th in the world. The first half looked likely to end scoreless until scrum-half Seren Lockwood scored in the 35th minute to give Wales a 7-0 lead at the break. Replacement Kelsey Jones drove over from a lineout, and Lockwood added a second try at the death.

Wales lost centre Freya Bell to a serious-looking knee injury during the match. The report described the performance as far from impressive, but said Sean Lynn's side had shown they can win ugly, with the bench making the difference. The two sides meet again in Kumagaya City next Saturday.

Wales ground out a win over Japan in tricky Tokyo conditions to secure a second victory of their WXV campaign. Swirling wind, rain and humidity made for a real battle between sides ranked 11th and 12th in the world, with a scrappy first-half looking likely to end scoreless.

But scrum-half Seren Lockwood's 35th-minute snipe gave the game a much-needed spark and the visitors a 7-0 advantage at the break. Wales lost centre Freya Bell to a serious-looking knee injury, but the impact of the bench proved the difference as Kelsey Jones drove over off a lineout ball, before Lockwood finished a rare moment of class at the death.

Rugby.copy:
Before England's three-match series against Canada, few would have predicted this outcome. A 2-0 series defeat for the Red Roses; their record 39-match winning streak and 41-match unbeaten run – stretching back nearly four years – ended; and consecutive losses for the first time since 2016.

Over the past 13 months, Canada have turned a 33-13 defeat in the World Cup final into a statement 31-22 win in Ottawa. And three years out from the 2029 World Cup, they have laid down an early marker of their title credentials.

Rugby.title: Red Roses suffer back-to-back defeats for first time in 10 years as Canada make statement
Rugby.summary: Red Roses suffer back-to-back defeats for first time in 10 years as Canada make statement The Guardian
bullets: England's Red Roses lost 31-22 to Canada in Ottawa in the WXV Global Series, their first consecutive defeats in a decade and only their third loss in 74 matches. Canada captain Sophie de Goede, the reigning world player of the year, scored a hat-trick, and Savannah Bauder also crossed. England replied through Maddie Feaunati, Amy Cokayne and Emma Sing, having trailed 12-7 at half-time.

England captain Meg Jones said the team is 'not broken, we just need to grow'. Head coach John Mitchell criticised the lack of a connection between referee Aurélie Groizeleau and the television match official. England finish the WXV series against the USA next Friday, while Canada's next games are slated for the 2027 Pacific Four tournament.
Rugby.copy:
History-makers, era-enders, giant-slayers. Breaking England’s unbeaten run was a statement for Canada last Friday but they backed it up in a 31-22 win to deal the Red Roses their first consecutive loss in a decade, sending a formidable message to the rest of world rugby.

Some may view it as too early to call but Canada are serious contenders for the World Cup trophy in 2029, especially if they progress at the same rate that their performances have improved in just a year from that World Cup final loss to England in 2025.

It followed Canada's 24-21 win in Toronto last weekend, which ended the Red Roses' 41-match unbeaten run, and gave Canada a 2-0 series win after a 26-26 draw in Exeter in September.

Head coach John Mitchell said England had become "a little bit predictable" and need a "new stimulus" in the new year. He also called for improved officiating standards after there was no television match official connection in the stadium, saying Jess Breach's disallowed interception try was a turning point. England face the USA in New Jersey next Friday, hoping to avoid three straight defeats for the first time since 2013.

Rugby.title: Impressive Gloucester beat Bath to extend lead at top of Prem
Rugby.summary: Gloucester storm to their first win over Bath in the Prem at Kingsholm since April 2022 with a 23-5 victory built on an immense defensive display.
Rugby.copy:
Gloucester stormed to their first win over Bath in the Prem at Kingsholm since April 2022 with a 23-5 victory built on an immense defensive display. The Cherry and Whites were down to 13 men for a period of the first half but led 9-5 at half-time, having repelled wave after wave of Bath pressure on their tryline.

George Barton then kicked three successive penalties to put the hosts 9-0 up before Kepu Tuipulotu pulled a try back just before the break from a driving maul. Freddie Thomas scored under the posts to stretch Gloucester's lead further midway through the second half and Max Llewellyn had Kingsholm raucous when he rolled over with two minutes to go for a famous victory that reaffirms their status as league leaders.

Rugby.title: Wade equals Ashton's Prem try-scoring record as Newcastle beat Sale
Rugby.summary: Christian Wade equals Chris Ashton's Prem try-scoring record with a 101st score as Newcastle post their first league win of their season against Sale.
bullets: Christian Wade equalled Chris Ashton's Premiership try-scoring record with his 101st try, scored in the right corner nine minutes into the second half. Newcastle Red Bulls beat Sale Sharks 17-3 at Kingston Park for their first league win of the season, with hooker George McGuigan adding a second try from a maul just after the hour.

The result was only Newcastle's fifth win in four Premiership seasons and leaves Harlequins as the only side yet to win this season. Sale, unbeaten in their previous two league games, scored only a George Ford penalty in blustery conditions. Newcastle coach Dan McFarland said there was no turning point and called it a long journey, adding that Wade deserves to take the record.
Rugby.copy:
Christian Wade equalled Chris Ashton's Prem try-scoring record with a 101st score as Newcastle Red Bulls posted their first league win of their season against Sale Sharks. On a blustery night dominated by kicking, penalties and stubborn defence, the match delivered a 17-3 win for the hosts and the try that Kingston Park wanted, with Wade going over in the right corner to draw level with Ashton nine minutes into the second period.

While a second eluded Wade in a game of few chances, George McGuigan managed to smuggle the ball over at the back of a maul as Newcastle stretched clear to post only a fifth win in four Prem seasons.

Rugby.title: Wallaroos complete Scotland sweep as retiring Smith gets standing ovation despite red
Rugby.summary: Wallaroos complete Scotland sweep as retiring Smith gets standing ovation despite red The Guardian
Rugby.copy:
The Wallaroos completed their three-game sweep over Scotland with a 38-31 win on Friday in a spicy contest that featured biting accusations and a string of yellow cards. Australia produced plenty of classy moments in Canberrabut again lacked discipline in tackles and around the ruck to keep the tourists in it. The hosts received four yellow cards, with the retiring centre Cecilia Smith earning two of those to finish her 34-Test career on a red.

Scotland had two players sent to the sin bin and it could have been far uglier if the Wallaroos centre Georgina Friedrichs’ accusations of biting had been verified on review. But the officials saw no evidence and there were no bite marks on Friedrich’s forearm, so the referee waved the complaints away.

Rugby.title: All Blacks legend Sonny Bill Williams undergoes life-saving surgery
Rugby.summary: All Blacks legend Sonny Bill Williams undergoes life-saving surgery Ruck.co.uk
bullets: All Blacks great Sonny Bill Williams, 41, has revealed he had open-heart surgery in Melbourne after doctors found a serious heart defect. He disclosed this in a 24-minute YouTube video titled My Heart Stopped. Doctors warned that his heart had grown to 7.5cm and was at risk of rupturing. Surgeon Dr Michael O'Keefe confirmed a Ross procedure to replace his aortic valve, and the operation was successful.

Williams said the recovery was frightening, describing the second day as the point when he thought he would not make it, and he suffered hallucinations afterwards. Doctors believe the condition may have affected his sporting career for years, and he said he had struggled with fitness from his late twenties. He won 58 Tests for New Zealand between 2010 and 2019, and two Rugby World Cups. He also won NRL titles in 2004 and 2013, played sevens at the 2016 Olympics and won the WBA International heavyweight title in 2013.
Rugby.copy:

Doctors warned Williams that his heart had grown to 7.5cm and was at risk of rupturing. “So, if I didn’t go in and get it checked, they wouldn’t know,” Williams explained. He added that a person could look perfectly healthy before suddenly dropping dead.

Rugby.summary: For many of the current Red Roses players, losing in an England shirt is an unfamiliar feeling.
bullets: England's Red Roses lost 24-21 to Canada at BMO Field in Toronto, ending a 41-match unbeaten run in front of a record crowd of 18,621. Back row Morwenna Talling, 24, who made her England debut in 2020 against Italy, said the defeat was "a bit gutting" but had to come eventually, and that England now have a chance to respond in a way they never have before.

The Red Roses face Canada again at TD Place in Ottawa on Friday in the third and final Test against them in the WXV Global Series, and then play the USA on 30 October. Talling said England let themselves down in finishing the pressure they built, and that Canada have developed, citing the pace of their backs in the wide channels. She added that the squad has been bonding off the pitch, including a team outing to an ice hockey game.
Rugby.copy:
For many of the current Red Roses players, losing in an England shirt is an unfamiliar feeling. Last weekend, Canada brought England’s impressive 41-match unbeaten run to an end, as they claimed a thrilling 24-21 victory at BMO Field in Toronto in front of a record-breaking crowd of 18,621 spectators.

For Morwenna Talling, who made her Red Roses debut in 2020 against Italy in a 54-0 win and has been a regular feature in the squad ever since, the defeat marked a rare low in an England career largely defined by success, but she is determined to help England bounce back when the two sides meet again in the WXV Global Series this weekend.

Rugby.title: WRU loses £18m and says four regions unsustainable
Rugby.summary: The Welsh Rugby Union blames rising energy and staffing costs combined with falling ticket sales for a dramatic drop in its finances.
bullets: The Welsh Rugby Union posted an £18m loss for the financial year to June 2026, against £7.2m the previous year, despite turnover rising £10m to £116.2m. It cited rising energy and staffing costs and falling ticket sales and fan spend, predicts a similar loss next year, and says the figures show four professional regions are unsustainable.

Chief financial and operating officer Gavin Marshall said costs include the stadium (£26m), national teams (£20m), loan interest (£3m) and community rugby (£4m), leaving about £20m for professional rugby against the £26m currently funded across four clubs. A £55m debt refinancing via HSBC and Goldman Sachs was agreed in January 2026. The WRU is also sustaining Cardiff's £1.2m loss, and the Ospreys and Scarlets are the regions threatened with closure.
Rugby.copy:
The Welsh Rugby Union has spelled out the "tough" economic state of the game in Wales - despite suggesting its financial position was "pretty good" just five months ago. The governing body has announced a significant decline in its finances, saying it has posted an £18m loss for the financial year to June 2026 - compared to a £7.2m loss the previous year.

Financial boss Gavin Marshall admitted the figures were disappointing and came despite turnover rising £10m to £116.2m. Just five months ago, new chief financial and operating officer Marshall claimed the WRU's finances were in a "pretty good position".

Head coach Sean Everitt said Van der Merwe has trained exceptionally well, but that it is too soon to discuss international selection before Scotland coach Gregor Townsend names his squad on Monday for the November Tests against New Zealand, Australia and Japan. Darcy Graham misses the game with a calf strain. The match follows the death of Lions lock Hyron Andrews, 31, from natural causes the day before their Champions Cup match at La Rochelle.

Van der Merwe had surgery on his ankle in order to be available for last year’s British and Irish Lions tour of Australia, but was never in serious contention for the Test matches despite five tries in five other games he played.

bullets: Australia coach Les Kiss has named a settled side for the first Bledisloe Cup Test against New Zealand at Eden Park on Saturday, keeping Joseph-Aukuso Suaalii on the left wing rather than restoring him to midfield. Rugby.copy:

The return of 27-year-old Henry is the only change to the starting side who upset South Africa 42-38 in Perth two weeks ago. Inside centre Hunter Paisami received a four-week ban for a high tackle against the world champions and is not available.

Rugby.title: Maro Itoje seals England future by agreeing new deal with Saracens
Rugby.summary: Maro Itoje seals England future by agreeing new deal with Saracens The Guardian
bullets: Maro Itoje has agreed a new deal with Saracens, believed to run until 2029, rejecting interest from Top 14 clubs, with Perpignan and Bordeaux among those mooted. His existing contract, signed in 2024, was due to expire after next year's World Cup. The 31-year-old, who has 102 caps, first played for the club in 2013.

Saracens' Brendan Venter, back in charge for a second time, said Itoje had agreed terms with the owner and described him as a brilliant leader. Itoje was rested for England's summer Tests against South Africa, Fiji and Argentina, and had his first full pre-season with Saracens since 2014. He was among the first players given an enhanced England contract, worth £150,000, in 2024, although none of the existing deals run beyond the World Cup in Australia next year.
Rugby.copy:
Maro Itoje has reaffirmed his long‑term commitment to England, rejecting interest from France by agreeing a new deal with Saracens. Itoje’s existing deal, signed in 2024, was due to expire after the World Cup next year but he has agreed terms with his club despite interest from Top 14 sides. A move to either Perpignan or Bordeaux had been mooted but the 31-year-old is to commit his future to the club he first represented in 2013 with a new deal, believed to be until 2029.

The extension is a significant boost for Saracens, who are in a period of transition with Brendan Venter at the helm for a second time and will enable Itoje, who has 102 caps, to continue his international career. It remains to be seen whether Steve Borthwick will still be in charge of the England side but either the national head coach or his successor is to benefit.

Rugby.title: ‘Freer’ Red Roses resolve to come back stronger after Canada end epic run
Rugby.summary: ‘Freer’ Red Roses resolve to come back stronger after Canada end epic run The Guardian
bullets: England's Red Roses suffered their first defeat in four years when Canada beat them, ending a run of 40 wins and one draw. The sides meet again this weekend. England have lost only twice in 73 matches over the past seven years.

Head coach John Mitchell, who lost his first game in charge, said a setback generally helps a team learn quicker and that the players may feel "freer" with the unbeaten run over. Captain Meg Jones said the key message was for the squad to stick together and respond. The loss, England's first away from home since the 2022 World Cup final, is seen as useful preparation for defending the title at the 2029 World Cup in Australia.
Rugby.copy:
England’s glittering unbeaten era is over. Canada defeated the Red Roses to deal them a first defeat in four years after 40 wins and one draw. It was a landmark result for the Canadians, who will look to replicate the outcome this weekend when the two nations meet again. England must reset but they won’t panic; the Red Roses have been the standard bearers for the past seven years, which is why they have lost only twice in 73 matches. But while no team would ever aim to lose, falling to defeat is a good thing for England and the wider sport.

Losing could actually make England a deadlier team to face. That is because they now need to find another level to their game with teams beginning to figure out ways to beat them. They have been pushed over the past few years by teams such as Canada, New Zealand and France, but they always had just enough to get the result over the line. Now they have been presented with a new challenge and John Mitchell, who lost his first game as Red Roses head coach, said post-defeat when his side “gets a setback, it generally learns quicker”.

Rugby.copy:

The defeat at BMO Field ended the Red Roses’ 41-match unbeaten run, their first loss since the 2021 Rugby World Cup final against New Zealand at Eden Park. Due to face Canada again this Friday night at Ottawa’s TD Place, the Red Roses have an opportunity to register an immediate response.

Rugby.title: Saracens owner backs CEO and rejects chaos claims
Rugby.summary: Saracens owner Dominic Silvester says he has full confidence in CEO Ed Coetzee, rejecting claims of "executive-level chaos".
bullets: Saracens owner Dominic Silvester has said he has "full confidence" in chief executive Ed Coetzee, rejecting a Times article that claimed the club was suffering "executive-level chaos". In an open letter on the club's website, Silvester said Coetzee had achieved an "extraordinary amount" since being appointed in July. The Times had pointed to Coetzee being the third chief executive in two years and alleged high staff turnover.

Silvester cited Coetzee's achievements, including bringing the all-female athletics meeting Athlos and the Mayo v Kerry Gaelic football fixture to StoneX Stadium, as well as new commercial and hospitality partnerships. He also highlighted a strengthened executive team, with Jason Thomas as chief financial officer and Rob Cook as chief operating officer, and said the board was committed to financial sustainability.
Rugby.copy:
Saracens owner Dominic Silvester says he has "full confidence" in chief executive Ed Coetzee and dismissed a newspaper article suggesting there was "executive-level chaos" at the club.

In an open letter on Saracens' website, external, responding to an article in The Times last week, Silvester said Coetzee had achieved an "extraordinary amount" since being appointed in July.

Rugby.title: Blitzboks go again with ‘target on our backs’
Rugby.summary: Blitzboks go again with ‘target on our backs’ News24
bullets: The 2026-27 SVNS Series opens in Dubai on 28 and 29 November, with the Cape Town leg the following weekend. The Blitzboks arrive as world champions for a second consecutive season, having won the title in June. They also won the league standings and five of the nine tournaments last season, including a second successive Cape Town victory.

Forward Zain Davids, who has played in 60 SVNS Series tournaments, said the team expects to carry a target as the top side, with rivals analysing them closely. The season also offers qualification for the 2028 Olympics in the United States: the top four in the World Championship standings qualify automatically, as do the winners of six continental tournaments. The 12th place goes to a last-chance qualifier, and the United States has already qualified as host.
Rugby.copy:
- The Blitzboks enter the new World Rugby Sevens season full of confidence following a successful campaign. - The new season starts at the end of the month in Dubai. - The home leg will once again be staged at Cape Town Stadium in December.

- For more rugby news, visit our dedicated section. Despite the many successes the Blitzboks have achieved over the past two seasons, there is no danger of the team getting carried away.

Rugby.title: Wales great Faletau still has drive for fourth World Cup
Rugby.summary: Wales boss Steve Tandy believes Taulupe Faletau is a World Cup contender despite missing out on the Nations Championship squad.
bullets: Wales head coach Steve Tandy believes number eight Taulupe Faletau, 35, is still driven by the prospect of a fourth World Cup. Faletau was left out of the squad for the Nations Championship after only returning from injury in Cardiff's Champions Cup defeat by Northampton on Sunday, where he played 55 minutes. He has 109 Wales caps but has not played under Tandy, and has not won a cap since facing Japan in the summer of 2025.

Tandy said he would not rule anyone out and had spoken to Faletau about being fit and available, but wants evidence of durability before a World Cup squad of 33 is chosen. Faletau has played only 31 times for Cardiff since joining from Bath in 2022. He could feature in November's Tests in Cardiff, and Cardiff host Sharks in the URC on Friday before facing Ospreys.
Rugby.copy:
Wales head coach Steve Tandy believes legendary number eight Taulupe Faletau is still fuelled by playing at a fourth World Cup. The 35-year-old was left out of Wales' squad for the Nations Championship, having only made his return from injury in Cardiff's Champions Cup defeat by Northampton on Sunday.

Faletau showed his class during a 55-minute appearance against the English champions but will remain with Cardiff rather than hunting a first cap since facing Japan in the summer of 2025.

Rugby.title: Jon Flatman: Cardiff Rugby appoint Barnsley FC chief executive as new CEO
Rugby.summary: Jon Flatman: Cardiff Rugby appoint Barnsley FC chief executive as new CEO BBC
bullets: Cardiff Rugby have appointed Barnsley FC chief executive Jon Flatman as their new CEO, with him due to start in January. The club have been without a full-time CEO since Richard Holland left the role 18 months ago, and managing director Jamie Muir will continue to lead the company until Flatman arrives.

Flatman said his priorities are taking the club back into private, independent ownership and resolving a long-term future at Cardiff Arms Park. Cardiff are still owned by the Welsh Rugby Union. He joined Barnsley in 2023 as chief revenue officer and became permanent CEO in 2024, helping to secure a long-term lease and development at Oakwell and sitting on the EFL board for League One clubs. Barnsley chairman Neerav Parekh said recruitment of a replacement is under way.
Rugby.copy:
Cardiff Rugby have appointed Barnsley Football Club's chief executive officer Jon Flatman as their new CEO. Flatman will assume the role in January and says he will prioritise securing private, independent ownership and establishing a long-term future at Cardiff Arms Park.

During his time at Barnsley, Flatman played a role in securing a long-term lease and development at Oakwell Stadium, and served on the English Football League (EFL) board as a representative of League One clubs.

Rugby.title: Five Wales stars not on flight to South Africa and Springbok's contract terminated
Rugby.summary: Five Wales stars not on flight to South Africa and Springbok's contract terminated Wales Online
bullets: The Scarlets have left five Wales internationals, Ryan Elias, Sam Costelow, Eddie James, Ellis Mee and Blair Murray, at home as the squad travelled to South Africa for United Rugby Championship matches against the Stormers in Cape Town on 24 October and the Bulls in Pretoria on 31 October. The club said the decision, agreed with the WRU, forms part of the player-management and rest provisions of PRA25 ahead of the Autumn Nations Championship.

The Scarlets travel with a 30-man squad, boosted by new signing Tom Allen and the return of prop Corey Domachowski. Separately, Springboks flanker Kwagga Smith, 32, has left Japanese club Shizuoka Blue Revs after eight seasons, with his contract terminated by mutual agreement as he recovers from injury. He joined in 2018 when the club were known as Yamaha Jubilo, and has won 63 caps for South Africa.
Rugby.copy:
Here are the latest rugby headlines this evening following the announcement of the Wales autumn squad. Five Wales internationals have been left at home by the Scarlets as the rest of the squad flew to South Africa today for matches against the Stormers and Bulls.

Ryan Elias, Sam Costelow, Eddie James, Ellis Mee and Blair Murray will miss the United Rugby Championship matches as part of planned recovery provisions agreed with the Welsh Rugby Union.

Rugby.title: Rugby Sevens set for historic return at Dakar 2026 Youth Olympic Games
Rugby.summary: Rugby Sevens set for historic return at Dakar 2026 Youth Olympic Games Primedia Plus
bullets: Rugby sevens will return to the Youth Olympic Games for the third time at Dakar 2026 in Senegal. The tournament starts on 1 November at the 8,000-seat Complexe Iba Mar Diop, one day after the opening ceremony on 31 October, with medals awarded on 2 and 3 November.

Eight men's and eight women's teams will be split into two pools of four. In the men's competition, hosts Senegal are in Pool A with South Africa, Canada and Germany, while Pool B features Argentina, France, Japan and Samoa. Dakar 2026 will be the first Olympic sporting event held in Africa, with around 2,700 athletes across 25 sports, and the first Youth Olympic Games to use the IOC's updated sports framework.
Rugby.copy:
Rugby ball resting on a field. Photo: Pexels/Pablo Hsm Dakar 2026 will make history as the first Olympic sporting event ever held on the African continent. Rugby sevens will return to the Youth Olympic Games for the third time when the world's best young players compete at Dakar 2026 in Senegal.

The tournament will kick off on November 1 at the 8,000-seat Complexe Iba Mar Diop, just one day after the opening ceremony on October 31. Medals will be awarded on November 2 and 3.

Rugby.title: The buzz of winning? No, Newcastle boss McFarland prefers Mondays
Rugby.summary: Newcastle Red Bulls head coach Dan McFarland on why winning cannot be the sole motivator for his group of players.
bullets: Newcastle Red Bulls head coach Dan McFarland, 54, says he prefers Mondays to Saturdays whether his side have won or lost, arguing that a professional's purpose cannot be winning alone. He took over a squad with 25 new players after the club finished bottom of the league in each of the last four seasons. They have lost all three opening Prem games but taken four bonus points, sitting ninth, two points above bottom side Harlequins.

McFarland said Mondays let him use the week's debrief and analysis to build an action plan for improvement, a view he formed as a player after moving from Stade Francais to Connacht. Ahead of Friday's game against Sale Sharks, he has shown his players footage of Michael Jordan's Chicago Bulls overcoming a 15-point fourth-quarter deficit against Portland Trail Blazers in the 1992 NBA Finals, to illustrate resilience.
Rugby.copy:
When we think of sport, the image that comes to mind is of incredible goals or brilliant tries or spell-bounding points that contribute to success. They are the things that stay with us, but as moments in themselves, they are fleeting, usually nothing more than a matter of seconds.

But the mantra we're lead to believe is that sport, especially at the highest level, is all about winning. Yet Newcastle Red Bulls head coach Dan McFarland is cut from a different cloth. For him, it is not winning but the constant search for self-improvement on an individual and team level that is his prime motivating factor.

bullets: Munster Rugby have confirmed that centre Alex Nankivell has signed a two-year contract extension, keeping him at the province until at least 2029. The uncapped 29-year-old joined from the Chiefs in the summer of 2023 and has made 58 Munster appearances. Last season he played 20 games and won three Player of the Match awards, and he also featured for the Barbarians against South Africa and Wales.

Nankivell won both the Bank of Ireland Men's Player of the Year and Virgin Media Supporters' Players of the Year awards at the 2026 Munster Rugby Awards. Munster general manager Ian Costello described him as a highly valued and respected squad member and said the club was delighted he had committed his future. Costello added that Nankivell has international ambitions and the club hopes he realises them in the near future.
Rugby.copy:
Munster Rugby have confirmed that centre Alex Nankivell has signed a two-year contract extension to keep him at the province until at least 2029. The uncapped 29-year-old joined Munster from the Chiefs in the summer of 2023 and immediately established himself as a key member of the squad.

Last season, Nankivell made a huge contribution and featured in 20 games, earning three Player of the Match awards. He capped off the season with appearances for the Barbarians against South Africa and Wales.

Rugby.summary: Scotland lock commits future to Glasgow Warriors as ‘easy decision’ explained Scotland Rugby News
bullets: Glasgow Warriors second-rower Alex Samuel has signed a new contract. The 23-year-old made his senior debut against Benetton in November 2022, has made 58 appearances for the club and was named Player of the Match in the 38-17 win over Leinster at Scotstoun in March.

Samuel came through Madras and Ayrshire Bulls before the Glasgow academy, captained Scotland U20 and made his senior international debut against Portugal in November 2024. He was picked for Scotland's summer tour of Argentina and South Africa and is now working back to full fitness. He said the decision to stay was easy given the club's direction, while head coach Franco Smith praised his physical edge and drive to improve.

Rugby.summary: Scotland staff member lands key role on historic British & Irish Lions tour Scotland Rugby News
bullets: Scotland Women's Head of Athletic Performance, Josie Symonds, has been appointed Head of Athletic Performance for the 2027 Women's British & Irish Lions tour of New Zealand. She will join head coach Jo Yapp's staff on secondment, moving into the role full-time from January 2027.

Symonds has been part of the Scotland Women set-up since joining Scottish Rugby ahead of the 2024 Six Nations, working through three Six Nations campaigns, WXV2 in South Africa in 2024, the 2025 Rugby World Cup and the current WXV Global Series. Rugby.summary: Exeter Chiefs Women have named vastly experienced Curtis Bradford as an assistant coach ahead of the new Premiership Women's Rugby season.
bullets: Exeter Chiefs Women have appointed Welshman Curtis Bradford as an assistant coach ahead of the new JAECOO Premiership Women's Rugby season. He arrives from Rugby Deutschland after three and a half years, most recently as director of rugby for the men's XVs programme and head coach of the Germany women's sevens squad.

Bradford will lead the defence and work closely with the backs at Sandy Park. His earlier roles include posts with the Welsh Rugby Union, Kuala Lumpur Tigers, NSW Waratahs and the Austrian Rugby Union. Head coach Oli Bishop said he wants a more aggressive, connected defensive side. Exeter finished third in PWR last season and lost their play-off to eventual champions Saracens; they begin 2026/27 against Bristol Bears at Shaftesbury Park on Saturday 28 November in Round 2.

bullets: Bath Rugby have confirmed that new signing Dan du Preez will miss the PREM matches away to Gloucester this Friday and at home to his former club Sale on Saturday 31 October. The 31-year-old injured his hamstring in training before last weekend's defeat to Montpellier in the Investec Champions Cup, having scored tries in both his appearances so far, against Harlequins and Exeter.

Miles Reid, who missed the Montpellier match with concussion, is nearing completion of his return-to-play protocol and is expected to be available this weekend. Sam Underhill is out until at least December with a bicep injury. Will Muir, Henry Arundell and Tom de Glanville have resumed elements of training. Billy Sela returns in late November, Jamie Bhatti is targeting the New Year, and Thompson Cowan is on track for the Autumn Prem Cup block, which begins away to Exeter on 7 November.
Rugby.copy:
Bath Rugby have confirmed that new signing Dan du Preez will miss the club’s next two PREM matches, the away trip to Gloucester this Friday and the clash at home to his former club Sale on Saturday 31 October.

Du Preez, who has had a solid enough start to his Bath career following a close-season move, injured his hamstring in training ahead of last weekend’s defeat to Montpellier in the Investec Champions Cup.

Roche, who can also play at 13, was in the Stormers side that faced the All Blacks on the Greatest Rivalry Tour this summer and received an invitation to a Springbok alignment camp in 2025. He could become a long-term successor to Bundee Aki, 36, or Robbie Henshaw, 33. Other South Africans have moved to Ireland, with Ulster signing Rynard Gordon and Josh Neill joining Leinster's Academy.

Hayter's immediate priority is the 2027 Women's Tour, followed by preparations for the 2029 men's tour. Head coach Jo Yapp said their experience would lay a foundation for the next 12 months.

Rugby.title: Unshackled Freeman in Christian Wade's rear mirror as record approaches
Rugby.summary: A purple patch of form has left Wade one short of Ashton's 101-try landmark going into Friday night's Northern derby against Sale Sharks at Kingston Park.
bullets: Newcastle Red Bulls winger Christian Wade is one try short of Chris Ashton's PREM record of 101 tries going into Friday night's Northern derby against Sale Sharks at Kingston Park. The 35-year-old reached 100 with a hat-trick against Exeter in the third round earlier this month. Ashton set the record in 2023 while at Leicester, having overtaken Tom Varndell's 92 tries in 2022.

Northampton and England winger Tommy Freeman is the main threat to the record in the longer term. He joined Wade on five tries this season with a brace in the 71-48 win over Bath, and has 60 PREM tries from 89 appearances, a try every 1.48 games, the best strike rate among players with 50 or more tries. Sam Simmonds is second on 1.54, Wade third on 1.56 and Max Malins fourth on 1.59. Freeman's club-mate Ollie Sleightholme has 45 tries from 70 appearances and needs five more to reach 50.
Rugby.copy:
It would would appear to be a case of when, not if, Newcastle Red Bulls flyer Christian Wade breaks Chris Ashton’s longstanding PREM try-scoring record. A purple patch of form has left Wade one short of Ashton’s 101-try landmark going into Friday night’s Northern derby against Sale Sharks at Kingston Park.

Just as Ashton did in 2023 whilst seeing out his career at Leicester, dual code winger Wade brought up his century with a hat-trick against Exeter in the third round earlier this month.

Rugby.title: ‘If the Bledisloe Cup must be a two-Test series, why not put it up for grabs every match?’
Rugby.summary: After New Zealand retained the trophy for a 24th straight year, is it time to change the format?
bullets: Calls are growing in Australia and New Zealand for a change to the Bledisloe Cup format, with the suggestion that the trophy be contested in every match between the two nations while the series remains at two Tests. Next year the series will revert to three matches, with the addition of an ANZAC Day Bledisloe Test in Brisbane. It was a four-match series from 2020 and from 2008 to 2010, and a two-match series from 1999 into the early 2000s.

Commentator Tony Johnson noted that the holder currently needs to win only one Test to retain the Cup, which he said swings the series heavily in the holder's favour. The article proposes two options: a one-off Bledisloe Test alongside two Rugby Championship games, or putting the Cup on the line in every match, as with the Ranfurly Shield in New Zealand. The Cup also went missing for three decades after 1949 before being found in a Melbourne storeroom in 1979.
Rugby.copy:
In the 90 years since its inception, the Bledisloe Cup has – to borrow from the great US sitcom Veep – maintained one common thread: continuity with change. Curiously, New Zealand Rugby and Rugby Australia can’t agree on whether it was first played for in 1931 or 1932. Both unions agree that Lord Bledisloe, the New Zealand Governor-General from 1930 to 1935, donated the giant trophy early in his reign, and unsurprisingly, both contend it was first played for when they won.

But since 1931 or 1932, the format has changed a lot. For the last few years, it has been played as a two-Test series. Next year, with the addition of the ANZAC Day Bledisloe Test in Brisbane, it will revert to the three-match series it was mostly through the 2010s.

Rugby.title: 'Haven't been showing up': Ex-All Black and Jeremy Paul lay into Wallabies after Bledisloe defeats
Rugby.summary: Former Wallabies hooker Jeremy Paul chimed in, agreeing with Read, admitting he turned the game off late in the contest.
bullets: Former All Blacks loose forward Kieran Read has criticised the Wallabies' showing in the Bledisloe Cup, saying they lacked character and have not been showing up. Les Kiss's side had gone unbeaten in his first five games in charge, including a win over the Springboks in Perth, before losing at Eden Park and then in front of a crowd of more than 73,000 at Accor Stadium in Sydney.

Speaking on The Good, The Bad & The Rugby Podcast, Read said the Wallabies were mentally off despite a nation backing them, and that structure matters less than turning up. Former Wallabies hooker Jeremy Paul agreed, saying he turned the television off late in the game for the first time in over a decade.
Rugby.copy:
Former All Blacks loose-forward Kieran Read has made his feelings clear about the Wallabies’ recent performances in the Bledisloe Cup, where Les Kiss’ side failed to turn hope into reality.

The Wallabies turned up to Eden Park with confidence after going unbeaten through Kiss’ first five games in charge, including an impressive victory over the Springboks in Perth.

Rugby.title: The two players that could be Les Kiss’s silver bullet
Rugby.summary: These are two genuine impact players and difference makers the Wallabies can no longer afford to ignore.
bullets: Wallabies coach Les Kiss has said "the time we have is the time that we have" as his side build towards the 2027 Rugby World Cup, after a heavy defeat to the All Blacks in Sydney. The Wallabies made 17 linebreaks, one more than New Zealand, but averaged only 0.9m post-contact per carry against the All Blacks' 0.7m. Across 2026 they have averaged about 2.3m, compared with South Africa's 3.2m and the All Blacks' 2.8m.

The article argues that Samu Kerevi and Langi Gleeson could add the carrying power Kiss wants. Gleeson has been named on Kiss's 'unavailable list' in each of four squad announcements. In Super Rugby Pacific 2025 he made 2.4m post-contact per carry, scored seven tries and beat 33 defenders, against 1.9m, one try and 27 for Rob Valetini. Montpellier said on 10 September that Gleeson, who has a knee injury, should return in about two months, in time for the April Bledisloe.
Rugby.copy:
The Wallabies have shown glimpses of physical dominance, attacking brilliance, and defensive pressure in 2026, but are yet to string together an 80-minute performance. It is now clear that while coach Les Kiss has been chopping and changing the side in a bid to build genuine competition and depth in the squad, you can’t rush an exercise which takes time: time which the Wallabies don’t have.

In the wake of the Wallabies walloping in Sydney at the hands of the All Blacks, Kiss was asked about the clock ticking until the home Rugby World Cup in 2027. “The time we have is the time that we have,” Kiss said.

Rugby.title: SVNS great says Bledisloe II offered ‘taste’ of Rugby World Cup 2027
Rugby.summary: All Blacks Sevens great Karl Te Nana is confident Men’s Rugby World Cup 2027 will be a massive hit in Australia.
bullets: More than 73,000 fans attended the second Bledisloe Cup Test of 2026 at Accor Stadium, the biggest Bledisloe crowd at the venue in 10 years. The All Blacks won 43-21, with Beauden Barrett and Josh Moorby scoring two tries each. All Blacks Sevens great Karl Te Nana said the atmosphere offered a taste of Men's Rugby World Cup 2027 in Australia.

The stadium will host two quarter-finals, both semi-finals, the bronze final and the final at the 2027 tournament, as well as Australia v New Zealand in the pool stage 357 days after Bledisloe II. World Rugby says 1.3 million tickets have been bought by fans from 164 countries. The tournament, which opens on 1 October 2027, will have 24 teams and 52 matches across seven host cities, with about 250,000 overseas visitors reportedly expected.
Rugby.copy:
All Blacks Sevens great Karl Te Nana is confident Men’s Rugby World Cup 2027 will be a massive hit in Australia, after more than 73,000 fans packed the stands at Accor Stadium for the second Bledisloe Cup Test of 2026.

Beauden Barrett and Josh Moorby scored two tries each as the All Blacks ran away with a 43-21 win at the Sydney venue, which will host two quarter-finals, both semi-finals, the bronze final and the Rugby World Cup Final at next year’s event.

Rugby.title: All Blacks take another step towards solving second-row puzzle
Rugby.summary: The All Blacks' second-row depth has been the cause of a persistent selection headache in 2026, but a stand-out performance in Sydney's second Bledisloe Test has left forwards coach Jason Ryan with nothing but praise for his starting duo.
bullets: All Blacks forwards coach Jason Ryan has praised the starting second-row pairing of Fabian Holland and Scott Barrett after the second Bledisloe Test in Sydney. Both missed the entire 2026 Super Rugby Pacific season through injury, Holland with a shoulder problem sustained in a pre-season game and Barrett with back trouble after returning from a sabbatical in May. Ryan said the starting front row and two locks were "massive" in the win.

Ryan said Holland was coming back into form after shoulder reconstruction, and that Barrett's return was a reward for his rehabilitation, with the World Cup under 12 months away. He also said the scrum operated at 100 per cent across the two-Test series. Ryan added that ball-in-play time was probably the biggest ever, which means the bench needs careful management.
Rugby.copy:
The All Blacks‘ second-row depth has been the cause of a persistent selection headache in 2026, but a stand-out performance in Sydney’s second Bledisloe Test has left forwards coach Jason Ryan with nothing but praise for his starting duo.

Both Fabian Holland and Scott Barrett missed the entire 2026 Super Rugby Pacific season due to injuries, with Holland sustaining a shoulder injury in a pre-season hit-out and Barrett running into back trouble as he looked to return from a non-playing sabbatical in May.

Rugby.title: HKCR MEN'S SEVEN SWEEP ASIA RUGBY SEVENS SERIES; WOMEN TAKE BRONZE
Rugby.summary: HKCR MEN'S SEVEN SWEEP ASIA RUGBY SEVENS SERIES; WOMEN TAKE BRONZE Hong Kong China Rugby
bullets: Hong Kong China Rugby's men won the Asia Rugby Emirates Sevens Series on 19 October, despite losing the Colombo cup final 28-14 to Japan. Hong Kong had won the opening leg in Suzhou, China, and reached both finals, earning a sixth straight Asian Sevens title on top of a third straight Asian Games gold earlier this month.

The women finished third overall in Asia, beating Kazakhstan 17-5 in the Colombo third-place match after a 17-7 semi-final loss to China. Nam Ka Man played her 50th tournament in Sri Lanka. Men's coach Jevon Groves said fatigue after the Asian Games was a factor, and the team will have a week off before preparing for the challenger event.
Rugby.copy:
[Hong Kong China, 19 October 2026]: Hong Kong China Rugby’s sevens athletes have concluded a successful Asian swing with the men sweeping the Asia Rugby Emirates Sevens Series today in Sri Lanka, while the women finished third overall in Asia as they maintained their momentum from the Asian Games.

The men suffered a rare loss in the cup final in Colombo, being well beaten by Japan, 28-14. Japan blitzed Hong Kong with two tries in the final two minutes of the first half and then opened the second with a quick score to lead 21-0 with three minutes remaining. A try from Max Denmark closed the gap to 21-7, but Japan replied quickly to push the lead out to 28-7 before Matt Worley scored late to close the gap to 28-14.

Rugby.title: How have Canada closed gap to world champions England?
Rugby.summary: Forty-one matches, four years and one Rugby World Cup triumph - but England's unbeaten run is over. So how did Canada close the gap to the Red Roses?
bullets: England's 41-match unbeaten run, which lasted nearly four years since 2022, ended with a 24-21 defeat by Canada in Toronto on Friday in front of a record home crowd of 18,621. It followed a 26-26 draw at Exeter's Sandy Park in September; before this autumn England had won all seven meetings between the sides this decade by an average margin of nearly 22 points.

Hooker Amy Cokayne said England were not "a million miles away" and that nothing needs to change massively. Canada head coach Kevin Rouet and many of his players have gained experience in England's PWR, and newer talents such as number eight Lizzie Gibson have emerged. England are without captain Zoe Stratford, Abbie Ward, Rosie Galligan and Marlie Packer, while Abby Dow has retired. The teams meet again on Friday in Ottawa.
Rugby.copy:
Forty-one matches, nearly four years and one Rugby World Cup triumph - but the Red Roses' unbeaten streak is over. It fell to the experienced Amy Cokayne to face the press this week after England lost their first match since 2022 against Canada.

"You can't dwell on it," said the Sale hooker, who has 95 international caps. "We weren't a million miles away, so it's not like we have to completely throw the book out - nothing needs to massively change to the way we play."

Rugby.title: Will Wales tackle reliance on Williams before World Cup?
Rugby.summary: Wales boast a world-class scrum-half in Tomos Williams but Steve Tandy might have to assess his back-up before the 2027 World Cup.
bullets: Wales scrum-half Tomos Williams has started every Test he has been available for since Steve Tandy took charge in summer 2025, playing past the hour in every outing. He played 378 minutes in the 2026 Six Nations, compared with 357 for France's Antoine Dupont, 323 for Ireland's Jamison Gibson-Park and 302 for Scotland's Ben White.

Williams has shared matchday squads with only two other scrum-halves, Kieran Hardy and Reuben Morgan-Williams, and Hardy faces a lengthy lay-off with a knee injury. Dragons' Che Hope, 23, is among the options, though Dragons defence coach Dale MacLeod urged caution. Gareth Davies, who retired from Test rugby in 2024 with 77 caps, has also been suggested as an emergency option. Wales open the 2027 World Cup against Zimbabwe in Adelaide on 2 October.
Rugby.copy:
There are few, if any, players more secure of a starting spot at next year's World Cup in Australia than Wales scrum-half Tomos Williams. France superstar Antoine Dupont has a rival for the nine jersey in Maxime Lucu, a talisman for back-to-back European champions Bordeaux-Begles.

Malcolm Marx, World Rugby player of the year, fights hard for his start as South Africa's hooker but must also be prepared for 'bomb squad' duty from the bench. The best players on the planet usually have a rival pushing them hard, but there is a gulf between 2025 British and Irish Lions tourist Williams and his fellow Welsh nines.

Racket.title: ATP doubles proposals: Players and legends sign open letter to prevent cuts
Racket.summary: ATP doubles proposals: Players and legends sign open letter to prevent cuts BBC
bullets: More than 150 men's doubles players, including British world number one Henry Patten and the Bryan brothers, have signed an open letter urging the ATP Tour to rethink proposals that would cut draw sizes and reduce prize money from 2028. The letter was signed on Monday by 137 current players, 28 legends and 20 national federations. The ATP has proposed halving doubles draws at Masters 1000 events to 16 teams, with smaller tournaments cut to eight teams, and the share of prize money going to doubles could fall from 20% to 10%.

The ATP board, made up of chairman Andrea Gaudenzi, four tournament representatives and four player representatives, will vote on the proposals at the ATP Finals in Turin next month. The ATP says the changes are based on data-led analysis of costs, revenue and viewership, and ATP sources insist a compromise is likely. Mike and Bob Bryan said they would support legal action, as in their 2005 lawsuit against the ATP over planned doubles changes.

Racket.summary: Jannik Sinner, Alexander Zverev earn over $1 million each in ATP’s record $18.3 million payout as Novak D The Times of India
bullets: Jannik Sinner and Alexander Zverev were the biggest beneficiaries of the ATP Tour's record $18.3m profit-sharing payout for the 2024 season, each earning more than $1m from Masters 1000 events. The ATP finalised the distribution on 3 October 2025, with 186 players who earned ranking points at the nine events qualifying. Sinner received $1,333,770 and Zverev $1,228,472, ahead of Andrey Rublev on $698,474.

The payout was 2.7 times the $6.6m distributed for 2023, while Novak Djokovic finished 12th with $403,641, outside the top 10. Under the 50-50 model introduced in 2022, profits above base prize money at Masters 1000 events are split equally between players and tournaments. The payments are separate from prize money and the $20.5m fixed bonus pool for the top 30 players.

The world No. 1 extended her winning streak to 50 matches, claimed a 10th title of the season and secured a third consecutive French Open crown, her fourth overall. She has won 66 of 67 matches this year.

The streak began after a 2-0 loss to China's Wang Zhiyi in the All England Open final in March. An played through an injury near her right Achilles tendon, sustained in the Denmark Open final, which medical examinations showed was not serious. She is expected to enter about three more tournaments this year, including the BWF World Tour Finals, and two more titles would beat her own single-season record of 11. She holds 48 career titles, past Susi Susanti's 46.

bullets: Malaysia will contest a record three finals at the French Open at Arena Grand Paris, the first time it has reached three finals at a single Super 750 event since the category began in 2018. Its previous best was two. In an all-Malaysian men's doubles final, world No. 11 Man Wei Chong-Tee Kai Wun face world No. 5 Goh Sze Fei-Nur Izzuddin Rumsani, guaranteeing a first Malaysian title since 2004.

Pearly Tan-M. Thinaah, world No. 4, face Japan's world No. 3 Yuki Fukushima-Mayu Matsumoto in the women's doubles, seeking successive World Tour titles after winning in Denmark last week. They beat Rin Iwanaga-Kie Nakanishi 21-17, 22-20 in the semi-finals. In the mixed doubles, world No. 31 Hoo Pang Ron-Lai Pei Jing meet China's top seeds Feng Yan Zhe-Huang Dong Ping, who beat them in the China Masters final last month.
Racket.copy:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia will contest a record three finals at the French Open later today, with one title already assured. Four pairs will carry the nation's challenge at Arena Grand Paris, marking the first time Malaysia has reached three event finals at a single Super 750 tournament since the category was introduced in 2018.

The country's previous best was two, achieved at the 2023 Denmark Open, last year's Japan Open, and last week's Denmark Open. In Denmark in 2023, Aaron Chia-Soh Wooi Yik claimed their first World Tour title by beating Indonesia's Muhammad Shohibul Fikri-Bagas Maulana 21-13, 21-17, while Lee Zii Jia finished as runner-up in the men's singles after losing to China's Weng Hong Yang 21-12, 21-6.

bullets: Aaron Chia and Soh Wooi Yik conceded a walkover to Man Wei Chong and Tee Kai Wun in the French Open men's doubles quarter-finals at the Arena Grand Paris, trailing 0-5 after two minutes. Coach Herry Iman Pierngadi said Wooi Yik injured his right leg in the first round against He Jiting and Ren Xiangyu, and the pair withdrew to avoid aggravating it. It was only their second tournament since reuniting, following a runner-up finish at the Denmark Open.

The withdrawal puts the world No. 4 pair's BWF World Tour Finals qualification at risk. They are seventh, holding one of eight places for the event in Hangzhou on 9-13 December, but are skipping the Hylo Open in Germany. Goh Sze Fei and Nur Izzuddin Rumsani beat world No. 1 Kim Won-ho and Seo Seung-jae 21-15, 21-18 to reach the semi-finals, and have already qualified for the Finals.

World No. 5 Sze Fei-Izzuddin stunned world No. 1 Kim Won-ho-Seo Seung-jae of South Korea 21-15, 21-18 to book their place in the semi-finals. Racket.title: An Se-young Dominates With 47th Title, Extends World No. 1 Reign
Racket.summary: An Se-young Dominates With 47th Title, Extends World No. 1 Reign 조선일보
bullets: The Badminton World Federation announced that An Se-young has set a record by winning her 47th international singles title, passing Indonesia's Susi Susanti, who won 46. The BWF's count covers only titles since 1999, when it began compiling statistics, and excludes team events such as the Uber Cup. An has won nine individual titles this season from 11 tournaments entered.

An has held the world number one ranking for 106 consecutive weeks, 168 in total, with 122,287 points. She has reached the semi-finals of the BWF World Tour France Open (Super 750) in Paris, beating China's Han Yue 21-13, 21-16 in the quarter-finals. A fourth French Open title would be her 10th of the year and the first three-peat at the event since Pi Hongyan won in 2003–2005.
Racket.copy:
[Sports Chosun Reporter Kim Ga-eul] Japan has praised An Se-young (Samsung Life Insurance), the "world's strongest," for her overwhelming skills. An Se-young is demonstrating formidable strength. She has won nine gold medals in individual events this season alone. Out of 11 international tournaments she participated in this season, she finished as runner-up at the All England Open, March, and withdrew in the round of 16 at the Japan Open, July, due to injury, but she claimed victory in all other events. An Se-young set a new record by reaching the top 11 times last year, tying the all-time single-season record for most wins in men's and women's singles with Kento Momota (Japan). At her current pace, she could set a new record.

The Badminton World Federation (BWF) officially announced, "An Se-young has set a new record by winning her 47th international singles title." The previous record was held by Indonesia's badminton "legend" Susi Susanti, who had 46 wins. However, the BWF's count of singles titles only includes records since 1999 when it began compiling statistics. Additionally, team event results such as the Uber Cup (World Women's Team Badminton Championships) or the Asian Team Championships are excluded.

Racket.title: Ashmita Chaliha Stuns Three-Time World Champion Akane Yamaguchi At French Open
Racket.summary: Ashmita Chaliha Stuns Three-Time World Champion Akane Yamaguchi At French Open News18
bullets: India's Ashmita Chaliha beat third seed and 2025 World Championships gold medallist Akane Yamaguchi 21-19, 21-18 in the second round of the French Open to reach the quarter-finals. It was the biggest win of her career. Chaliha, who won the Korea Masters earlier this year, had lost to Yamaguchi in the Denmark Open round of 16 last week, and had beaten China's Han Qian Xi 21-18, 24-22 in round one.

She will face either 11th seed Pornpawee Chochuwong or Nozomi Okuhara in the last eight. PV Sindhu also reached the quarter-finals, beating Riko Gunji in straight games, and will meet Chiu Pin-Chian or Sim Yu Jin. Elsewhere it has been a difficult week for Indian players: Treesa Jolly and Gayatri Gopichand, Satwiksairaj Rankireddy and Chirag Shetty, Unnati Hooda, Devika Sihag, Tanvi Sharma and Ayush Shetty all went out, and Lakshya Sen conceded a walkover.
Racket.copy:
Ashmita Chaliha produced the biggest victory of her career, stunning world champion and third seed Akane Yamaguchi in straight games to reach the French Open quarterfinals. Star Indian women’s singles shuttler Ashmita Chaliha, who won the Korea Masters earlier this year, stunned the 2025 World Championships gold medallist and third seed Akane Yamaguchi in the second round of the French Open to pull off the biggest win of her career.

Racket.summary: Tennis | ATP Brussels 2026 | Fearnley brushes aside Gaston to set Chidekh second round clash Britwatch Sports
Racket.copy:
BRUSSELS, BELGIUM – Jacob Fearnley cruised past Hugo Gaston in straight sets to set up a second round meeting with Clement Chidekh. A big win for Jacob Fearnley over Hugo Gaston means he is into the second round in Brussels where Clement Chidekh now awaits.

Fearnley will aim to serve aggressively in what is a tricky opening round match against Chidekh. Despite not having the best record on other surfaces, Chidekh has a tremendous record on indoor hard courts. The Frenchman has won Challenger and ITF events on the surface with Fearnley knowing more than most how much of a threat Chidekh can be with the Frenchman beating the Brit at a Challenger event earlier this season. Now, Chidekh aims to repeat the feat and produce a big win in his season as he has huge aspirations ahead of 2027.

Racket.title: Boulter wins in under an hour to reach quarters
Racket.summary: Katie Boulter moves into the quarter-finals of the Japan Open after she beat Viktorija Golubic in less than an hour.
bullets: Katie Boulter reached the quarter-finals of the Japan Open in Osaka with a 6-2 6-1 victory over Switzerland's Viktorija Golubic in less than an hour. The eighth seed won nine games in a row from 2-2 in the first set, and Golubic took only the penultimate game of the match.

Boulter will face either Croatia's Antonia Ruzic or American Kayla Day in the next round. The 30-year-old lost the British number one ranking to Sonny Kartal on Monday but is set to retake it following her run this week. She said she was pleased to stay patient in difficult, windy conditions and felt she played some really good tennis in the second set.

Katie Boulter moved into the quarter-finals of the Japan Open after she beat Viktorija Golubic in less than an hour. The British number two defeated her Swiss opponent 6-2 6-1 in Osaka and will face either Croatia's Antonia Ruzic or American Kayla Day in the next round.

Boulter saved a break point in the opening game but dominated from 2-2 in the first set, winning nine games in a row before Golubic took the penultimate game of the match. The 30-year-old lost the British number one spot to Sonny Kartal on Monday, but is set to retake the position following her run this week.

Racket.summary: Six-time Grand Slam champion Iga Swiatek ends her 2026 season after failing to qualify for the WTA Finals for the first time since 2019.
bullets: Iga Swiatek has ended her 2026 season early, pulling out of the Ningbo Open with a thigh injury and missing the WTA Finals for the first time since 2019. The 25-year-old six-time Grand Slam champion has dropped to ninth in the rankings and will return in 2027, saying she needs to rest and recover after two intense years.

She won one title this year, the Canadian Open in Toronto in August, and finished with a 42-16 record, her first season without a Grand Slam title since 2021. She split with coach Wim Fissette in March and appointed Francisco Roig, and lost to Maja Chwalinska in the Wuhan Open semi-finals. She can complete the career Grand Slam at the Australian Open in January.
Racket.copy:
Six-time Grand Slam champion Iga Swiatek has called an early finish to what she described as "one of the most challenging" seasons of her career. Poland's Swiatek failed to qualify for the end-of-season WTA Finals - for the first time since 2019 - after pulling out of the Ningbo Open on Tuesday with a thigh injury.

Shortly afterwards, the 25-year-old announced she was bringing a largely barren season to a close, in order to recharge over a longer period of time before returning in 2027. Former long-time world number one Swiatek - who has ended a season without a Grand Slam title for the first time since 2021 - has dropped to ninth in the rankings.

It was Bergs’ third career win over a top 10 player, but his first against an opponent ranked in the top three. He had lost his only previous encounter against Alcaraz at the 2025 Japan Open.

Golf.copy:
Austin Smotherman claimed his second PGA Tour title with a Monday play-off victory over Seamus Power at the weather-hit Bermuda Championship. The 32-year-old American parred the third extra hole to fend off the Irishman and seal his second tournament win in as many starts after a breakthrough victory in Utah earlier this month.

Smotherman and Power contested the sudden-death play-off on Monday after inclement weather forced organisers to cancel Sunday's scheduled final round. With more bad weather forecast on Monday, officials decided to scrap the final round and proceed with a play-off between the 54-hole leaders.

Golf.title: Bermuda Championship: Austin Smotherman beats Seamus Power in Monday play-off for second PGA Tour win
Golf.summary: Bermuda Championship: Austin Smotherman beats Seamus Power in Monday play-off for second PGA Tour win BBC
bullets: Austin Smotherman won the Bermuda Championship on Monday, beating Seamus Power at the third hole of a sudden-death play-off for his second PGA Tour title, following his first victory in Utah earlier this month. Weather forced the cancellation of the final round, so officials went straight to a play-off between the 54-hole leaders, who were both on 16 under.

Smotherman, 32, shot 65, 66 and 66, while 2022 champion Power had 66, 64 and 67. Power missed a 20-footer on the first play-off hole, the par-three 16th at Port Royal, before Smotherman two-putted from 15 feet at the third. Power's runner-up finish effectively secures his 2027 PGA Tour card: he entered the week 103rd in the FedEx Cup Fall standings and is projected to rise to 53rd, with the top 100 earning cards.

bullets: Jon Rahm received $26m from LIV Golf in the year before the league filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection on 8 September, court records filed in New Jersey show. Bryson DeChambeau was paid nearly $13.9m and Dustin Johnson $10.7m, while LIV also paid seven executives $15.6m in retention money. Chief executive Scott O'Neil received more than $13.6m between September 2025 and August 2026.

Contractors including Fresh Tape Media ($1.23m), Mobii Systems (over $1.1m) and Deltatre (nearly $860,000) say they are still owed money, and players are among the largest unsecured creditors, with Rahm owed about $7.5m. Rahm has reached a separation agreement releasing LIV from monetary claims, which a judge is due to consider on 5 November. Golf.copy:

The figures are in documents filed late Thursday in the U.S. Bankruptcy Court in New Jersey, where LIV sought Chapter 11 protection on Sept. 8. The payments to players also include nearly $13.9 million to American Bryson DeChambeau, the 2024 U.S. Open champion, and $10.7 million to Dustin Johnson, a former world No. 1. Australian Cameron Smith and American Bubba Watson each received about $2.5 million.

Golf.copy:
HAENAM, South Korea (AP) — Yuri Yoshida won the LPGA South Korea tournament holding off Haeran Ryu and Hye-Jin Choi in a close finish at Pine Beach Golf Links on Sunday. It was Yoshida’s first LPGA Tour victory and came in dramatic finale as both overnight leader Haeran Ryu and Yoshida bogeyed the final hole leaving the Japanese player ahead by one stoke and a four-round total of 17-under 271.

Yoshida was four shots off the pace going into Sunday’s final round but lit up the front nine with an eagle at the par-5 second, followed by three consecutive birdies to be 5-under 31 at the turn. Bogey’s at the 15th and 18th was offset by a crucial birdie at the 17th which gave the 26-year-old the buffer she needed.

bullets: LIV Golf paid $15.6m in retention payments to executives before filing for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection, according to court documents. CEO Scott O'Neil received a $6.375m retention bonus on 24 June and was paid more than $13.6m between 12 September 2025 and 28 August 2026. CFO David Phillips was paid more than $3.3m and chief legal officer John Ruzich about $2.6m, while founding commissioner Greg Norman received more than $9.4m when he left in September 2025.

The payments came as LIV failed to pay vendors, prompting lawsuits including Fresh Tape Media seeking $1.23m and Mobii Systems claiming more than $1.1m. The filings also show Cameron Young signed an intent to play for LIV after the 2022 Open. The deadline for players to commit to LIV 2.0 is Sunday 25 October. A LIV attorney told the court the league expects to know by the end of the month whether it will proceed, with up to $300m of financing from BC Partners.

Golf.title: LIV's latest court filings paint clearest picture of league's lavish spending
Golf.summary: LIV Golf's most recent bankruptcy court filings are a reminder of just how much money it takes to run a flashy golf league. The post LIV’s latest court filings paint clearest picture of league’s lavish spending appeared first on Golf .
Golf.copy:
Bankruptcy filings are notoriously cumbersome, but every bankruptcy judge would admit the tedious paperwork is necessary. If a company is declaring bankruptcy, and thereby seeking some sort of legal protection against its current state, it had better be able to explain why.

But the process of doing so is a nightmare for lawyers as much as it is for their printers. It doesn’t take long for the number of pages to cross the threshold of tens of thousands. On Thursday evening alone, thousands of pages were filed in LIV Golf’s bankruptcy case, across its lot of international entities, its 13 franchises and dozens of other subsidiaries. Staring at it might send you into a daze, but there’s plenty that can be gleaned from these documents, which were prepared by LIV’s management and advisors. Thursday’s trove offered one main theme: LIV Golf owed many companies money.

bullets: Tiger Woods hopes to play a full TGL schedule this season and could return to competition before the end of 2026, according to former Jupiter Links GC team-mate Kevin Kisner. Woods has not played on the PGA Tour since missing the cut at The Open in July 2024, and made only one TGL appearance last season because of injury.

Woods is listed in Jupiter Links' expanded five-player roster for 2026/27, with Keith Mitchell replacing Kisner. The new TGL season, which has a seventh team, begins on 27 December, live on Sky Sports. Kisner expects Woods to play the Hero World Challenge in the Bahamas and the PNC Championship, though Woods was not in the initial Hero field and could still enter via a sponsor's exemption. In September Woods received a five-year driving suspension after a plea agreement on a reckless driving charge over March's car crash.

Golf.summary: Golfer on the verge of tears as DP World Tour withdrawal has major consequences talkSPORT
bullets: Thailand's Kiradech Aphibarnrat, 37, lost his DP World Tour card for 2027 after withdrawing from the Genesis Championship at Woo Jeong Hills Country Club in South Korea. He began the week 106th in the Race to Dubai Rankings, with only the top 100 guaranteed Category 10 status, and was five over par after nine holes of round two following an opening 75.

Aphibarnrat apologised to fans and said the last three or four years had been difficult, adding that playing 11 straight weeks to retain his card had left him drained. He plans to return to Qualifying School in Spain next month, where he won his card back in 2022 and 2023. His career-high world ranking was 29th in 2018, and his last major appearance was the 2019 Open Championship.

Golf.copy:
Long-time PGA Tour pro Joel Dahmen has welcomed the sweeping changes planned for 2028 but believes veterans could face an uphill battle to remain competitive. The North American circuit is moving to a two-tier structure in two years' time, with the introduction of a Championship and Challenger Series.

Players will switch level at the end of the season based on performance. Golfers who win twice on the second tier will earn automatic promotion. The new model was approved by the Tour's policy board in June and is designed to keep the world's leading players together more consistently and increase the consequence of poor performance.
