Golf.summary: Race To Dubai Update: Can Casey Jarvis Make It A Four Horse Race? Golf Monthly
bullets: Eugenio Chacarra's victory at the DP World India Championship took him above Rory McIlroy and Patrick Reed to the top of the Race to Dubai rankings. Casey Jarvis, fourth before the Genesis Championship in Korea, led after day one and could climb to third with a top-two finish, or to second with a win.

Points rise sharply in the closing DP World Tour Play-Offs in Abu Dhabi and Dubai, where the title will be decided. McIlroy is chasing a record-equalling eighth Race to Dubai title, while Reed would become only the second American winner. Jarvis, 23, won the Magical Kenya Open and South African Open early in the season, and Chacarra, a former LIV Golf player, won the KLM Open and Open d'Italia in June.
Golf.copy:
It was supposed to be a two-horse race between big guns Rory McIlroy and Patrick Reed before Eugenio Chacarra's surging form saw him muscle in on the act. But that three-way battle could become a four-strong contest heading into the DP World Tour Play-Offs if Casey Jarvis can back-up a fine start at the Genesis Championship in Korea.

After a couple of near misses, Chacarra's victory at the DP World India Championship saw the Spaniard overtake both McIlroy and Reed to climb to the top of the points rankings.

bullets: Bryson DeChambeau has been confirmed for the Nedbank Golf Challenge at Sun City, South Africa, on 3-6 December, where he will face Justin Rose, Marco Penge and defending champion Kristoffer Reitan. It will be his first non-Major DP World Tour start since 2022 and his first competitive action since the LIV Golf finale in August. Gary Player had announced his entry in August.

ESPN has reported that DeChambeau remains committed to LIV Golf and is working to bring LIV Golf 2.0 to life. A 25 October deadline applies for chief executive Scott O'Neil to sign enough players, as a $300m investment from BC Partners depends on the number and quality of signings, although the deadline could be extended. DeChambeau had reportedly spoken to the DP World Tour about more starts next season, but Guy Kinnings has said players must choose one tour or the other.
Golf.copy:
Bryson DeChambeau has confirmed his appearance at December's Nedbank Golf Challenge on the DP World Tour, but he is reportedly still focused on helping LIV Golf 2.0 become a reality.

The two-time US Open champion was announced as an entrant for 'Africa's Major' back in August by Gary Player himself - and now the tournament has confirmed his appearance. The Nedbank Golf Challenge in honour of Gary Player will take place at Sun City from 3-6 December where De Chambeau will take on the likes of Justin Rose, Marco Penge and defending champion Kristoffer Reitan.

Golf.title: Nelly Korda could wrap up LPGA Player of the Year while sitting at home
Golf.summary: Nelly Korda could wrap up LPGA Player of the Year while sitting at home Golfweek
bullets: Nelly Korda could clinch the LPGA's Rolex Player of the Year award while on a two-month break from the tour. The world No. 1 leads South Korea's Haeran Ryu by 75 points. If the gap exceeds 60 points after the Toto Japan Classic, Korda will clinch mathematically with two events remaining. Ryu would need three wins, or two wins, a second-place and an eighth-place finish, to overtake her.

The award carries one LPGA Hall of Fame point, and Korda, 28, has 25 of the 27 needed for induction. She won four of her first eight events this season, including the first two majors, while Ryu won the next two. Jeeno Thitikul needs three wins and Miyu Yamashita four to overtake Korda. Korda clinched the award with two events left in 2024, and the race has been decided at the CME Group Tour Championship seven times in the last 10 years.
Golf.copy:

On Wednesday, longtime LIV captain and former major champion Louis Oosthuizen announced his departure from LIV Golf, dealing the latest blow to the league’s future. Oosthuizen joins Jon Rahm as the most notable LIV players to publicly confirm their exits from the league. And while Rahm is a far better player than Oosthuizen, and his decision to leave far more impactful, Oosthuizen’s importance to the league should not be overlooked.

He captained the Southern Guards team for LIV’s entire existence. That team was made up entirely of South African pros, and LIV’s South Africa tournament has been one of its biggest success stories. Furthermore, Oosthuizen’s success in major championships, including his 2010 Open Championship victory and a pile of high finishes, raised the stature of the league.

Golf.title: Another major champion set for LIV exit
Golf.summary: Another major champion set for LIV exit Irish Golfer Magazine
bullets: Louis Oosthuizen has said he will not continue in LIV Golf's planned next iteration, becoming the latest major champion set to leave the league. The 2010 Open champion told the South China Morning Post at the Asian Tour's Link Hong Kong Open that the travel schedule would be too demanding for his body at 44, and confirmed his decision in a statement on Instagram.

Oosthuizen joins Jon Rahm, who has ruled himself out of LIV next season, while Sergio Garcia's contract was terminated in the courts, though he could still re-sign. Brooks Koepka and Patrick Reed left before the 2026 season, meaning seven major winners had already departed. The league's future remains uncertain despite BC Partners' pledge to invest, and Oosthuizen, who played for Southern Guards GC, said he would prefer to play three weeks at a time in one location.
Golf.copy:
With LIV Golf’s future shrouded in doubt despite BC Partners’ pledge to invest, another major champion has declared himself out of whatever form the league continues in. Jon Rahm has already ruled himself out of being a LIV player next season, and Sergio Garcia has had his contract terminated in the courts though could still re-sign before the start of next season. Brooks Koepka and Patrick Reed left before the start of the 2026 season, meaning that a total of seven major championship wins had already made their way to the exit.

And now Louis Oosthuizen looks set to make it eight. The 2010 Open champion is in Hong Kong for the Asian Tour’s Link Hong Kong Open and he told the South China Morning Post that he has no plans to continue playing in LIV 2.0 should it get off the ground as he expects that the travel schedule will be too much for the 44-year-old’s body.

Golf.title: I had one of my best competitive years in 2026. Here's how my gear helped me
Golf.summary: This past year was one of my best competitive seasons, and it came after I made wholesale changes to my golf bag. The post I had one of my best competitive years in 2026. Here’s how my gear helped me appeared first on Golf .
Golf.copy:
This past year, I had perhaps my best competitive season since high school, and a big reason was the new trust I had in my equipment. This season, I shot 71 twice, made an albatross, got my handicap index back below 1.0, and qualified for my first state amateur or mid-amateur in five years. The journey started, though, when we embarked on Fully Fit, a fitting bonanza that gave me the chance to get fit by six OEMs and decide what clubs would make it into my bag for the upcoming year. While I had been GOLF’s gear editor for about a year, I still had yet to take that kind of holistic look at my entire golf bag with each OEM. In fact, at that point, I had had a full bag fitting with just two of them.

It’s not so much that I had any gaping holes in my bag, but there was so much I hadn’t tried. While many of my fittings ended up in product that I would have expected, other spots I tried something new.

He finished on 17-under 263 at The Renaissance Club in North Berwick and won by two shots from Min Woo Lee. It was the fourth PGA Tour title of his career and ended a wait of 1,001 days since his last win.

Kim pointed to one early swing on Sunday as the key to his round. On the second hole, playing into the wind, he hit a 2-iron to seven feet. He missed the birdie putt, but the quality of the shot told him something special could happen.

Golf.title: Rory McIlroy backs a possible PGA Tour return for select LIV Golf players
Golf.summary: Rory McIlroy backs a possible PGA Tour return for select LIV Golf players Yahoo Sports
bullets: Rory McIlroy said at the Bloomberg New Economy Forum in New Delhi on 13 October that he would vote to welcome former LIV Golf players back to the PGA Tour and DP World Tour. He argued their return could improve the tours' business prospects and strengthen their fields, while criticising how LIV used its financial resources. He acknowledged that not all players would share his view.

LIV's future is uncertain after Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund said it would end its funding after the 2026 season and the league entered Chapter 11 proceedings. BC Partners received court approval for up to $300 million in financing, and a decision on LIV 2.0 is expected by the end of October. DP World Tour chief executive Guy Kinnings has said players in LIV 2.0 in 2027 cannot compete on the European circuit. The PGA Tour's Returning Member Program, introduced in January 2026, carries a $5 million charitable contribution, and CEO Brian Rolapp said in August there were no plans to revive it.
Golf.copy:
Rory McIlroy has signaled a willingness to welcome former LIV Golf players back to the PGA Tour, adding a significant twist to professional golf's ongoing divide. The Northern Irish star, once among the breakaway league's most outspoken critics, now believes bringing certain players back could strengthen the tour commercially and competitively.

His latest comments arrive as LIV Golf confronts serious financial uncertainty and several prominent players reassess their futures. However, McIlroy's support doesn't amount to an unrestricted invitation for every former rival. Questions about eligibility, financial consequences, and the views of current PGA Tour members remain central to any potential reintegration.

Golf.title: How shared stewardship helps drive the game forward
Golf.summary: There's more golf around us than ever. Here's why we need to embrace these additional forms while also creating pathways into more traditional golf. The post How shared stewardship helps drive the game forward appeared first on Golf .
Golf.copy:
This piece was first published on the USGA’s website. In 2009, World Golf Hall of Famer Tom Watson, then 59, was on the verge of becoming the oldest major champion in history. After a nearly perfect iron shot into the 18th green landed firmly and rolled over the putting surface, Tom made bogey and lost in a playoff. Even so, it was an incredible runner-up finish.

Over the years, Tom and my dad, the longtime head golf professional at Delray Dunes Golf & Country Club, forged a strong friendship. Dad wanted to congratulate him on his inspiring performance. Knowing Tom had likely received hundreds of messages, I thought it unlikely we would ever hear back from him following his legendary near-miss.

bullets: TGL announced the full rosters for its third season on Tuesday, with Motor City GC joining as the league's seventh franchise. Golf.copy:
TGL, the simulator golf league co-founded by Tiger Woods and Rory McIlroy, returns this winter for its third season after a successful inaugural campaign that proved the concept and a second season that added new holes, tweaked gameplay and built momentum.

TGL’s third season will see a new team enter the mix, too, as Motor City GC will be the league’s seventh franchise. On Tuesday, TGL announced the complete rosters for its third season, and there have been some changes along with the introduction of Motor City GC. Before, teams had four players on a roster, with three participating each week. Now, teams will have five players, but still only three players will tee it up for each match at the SoFi Center in Florida.

Golf.title: Hero World Challenge field announced, but will Tiger Woods play?
Golf.summary: The field for the 2026 Hero World Challenge is mostly set, although there are still spots available if the host, Tiger Woods, wants to play. The post Hero World Challenge field announced, but will Tiger Woods play? appeared first on Golf .
bullets: Seven of the world's top 10 players will compete at the Hero World Challenge, hosted by Tiger Woods, at Albany in the Bahamas on 3-6 December. Scottie Scheffler, Matt Fitzpatrick and Cameron Young headline the field. Only 17 of the 20 players were announced on Monday, with three places left as "TBA tournament exemption" spots.

Woods is not yet in the field, but he could take one of the exemptions, as he has done in some previous years. He has not played competitively since missing the cut at the 2024 Open Championship, and he last played the Hero in 2023. He ruptured his Achilles in March 2025 and had a back disc replacement in October 2025. He has also been named on the TGL season three roster, as captain of Jupiter Links.
Golf.copy:
The field for this year’s Hero World Challenge is mostly set, with few surprises, although now the big storyline is if the tournament host will tee it up as well. Seven of the top 10 players in the world will compete at the Tiger Woods-hosted Hero World Challenge Dec. 3-6 at Albany in the Bahamas, and no, Woods is not in the 20-player field. At least not yet.

While it wouldn’t be surprising if Woods sat this one out, only 17 players were announced Monday, with three spots remaining for a “TBA tournament exemption.” Leaving a few spots available for last-minute exemptions is typical for the Hero, and it also makes it convenient for Woods to snag one himself — without kicking a player out — if he’s satisfied with his health and game. In past years Woods has used one of these exemptions on himself, but other times he’s passed on it.

Golf.title: You can now (finally) play this once off-limits Wyoming stunner
Golf.summary: New accommodations at Snake River Sporting Club offer guests a way on to a spectacular Tom Weiskopf design. The post You can now (finally) play this once off-limits Wyoming stunner appeared first on Golf .
Golf.copy:
Early in your round at Snake River Sporting Club, you pass a wooden cabin about the size of a turnstand. No snacks are on sale here. It’s only the 3rd hole, you don’t need them yet. The cabin is a relic: evidence that homesteaders were here before Tom Weiskopf, before the club, before any of this was given over to golf.

In the early 1800s, this swath of land alongside the Snake River, south of what is now Jackson Hole, Wyo., was fertile ground for the fur trade. Prospectors of other stripes came later, settling down and building infrastructure of all kinds, including that modest wooden cabin. Another century passed before Weiskopf arrived. The former major champion-turned-course architect drew up a routing that became the centerpiece of an exclusive golf club. The course opened in 2006, making it much younger than the cabin. Like the cabin, though, it fits the landscape. It looks as if it’s been there all along.

Golf.copy:
LIV Golf burst onto the professional golfing scene back in June 2022 with one sole ambition: to topple the PGA Tour. The powers that be at LIV Golf may dispute that statement, but it was obvious for everyone to see that they wanted to end the PGA Tour.

bullets: A significant number of LIV Golf players are negotiating contracts with the DP World Tour that would let them bypass Q School and guarantee tournament starts in 2027, on condition that they do not sign up to LIV's proposed relaunch. Some players without DP World Tour status would be offered a set number of sponsors' invites based on their value to the circuit. LIV players cannot hold DP World Tour memberships if they join the next iteration of the league.

Three-time DP World Tour winner Sam Horsfield has entered Second Stage of Q School at Isla Canela Links, which may make him ineligible for such a deal. Josele Ballester, Luis Masaveu and Michael La Sasso, who all came through the First Stage, are also in the field. The second stage runs from 29 October to 1 November across four Spanish venues, and the Final Stage the following week at Infinitum will offer 20 DP World Tour cards.
Golf.copy:
As LIV Golf’s deadline looms, a number of the league’s players are working towards securing a different kind of playing future in 2027. TG revealed earlier this month that a significant number of LIV stars are negotiating contracts with the DP World Tour that will enable them to bypass the circuit’s gruelling Q School and guarantee them a tournament starts next season – on the condition they don’t sign up to the league’s proposed relaunch.

Some players without status on the DP World Tour will be offered a certain number of sponsors invites, based on their perceived value to the circuit, filling out blank schedules if they reject the terms offered by LIV 2.0.

Golf.title: LIV Golf survival bid heats up ahead of looming 2.0 deadline
Golf.summary: LIV Golf survival bid heats up ahead of looming 2.0 deadline bunkered.co.uk
bullets: LIV Golf has until 25 October to secure player commitments to its 2.0 restructuring, after an earlier 13 October deadline was extended. The league lost Saudi Public Investment Fund backing in April, and BC Partners Credit has agreed to invest up to $300 million to continue it into 2027. Bunkered understands the deadline can be extended or waived by BC Partners, and that the amended agreement now requires a "critical mass of players" rather than fixed numerical thresholds.

LIV's counsel told a New Jersey bankruptcy court that a decision on whether 2.0 goes ahead will come by the end of October. Jon Rahm has confirmed he will leave, while Bryson DeChambeau, a free agent after his contract was rejected in the Chapter 11 proceedings, is understood to have spoken with the new investors. The DP World Tour has told players they can no longer compete on both circuits, with CEO Guy Kinnings saying players need to make a choice.

Golf.copy:
Your golf bag works harder than almost anything else you own. It hauls 14 clubs (15 if nobody’s looking), dozens of balls, a rangefinder, a rain jacket and whatever snack and drink stash you opt to carry. And it does it every round. If we’re being honest, most of us probably don’t think about our bag until something goes wrong: a zipper that sticks, a strap that digs in, a divider that lets your irons clang together.

Then there’s the summer. Months of heat and direct sun fade fabric, wear down zippers, and weaken stitching. Sweaty hands and wet-weather rounds leave their mark too. Your bag that felt fine in May can be pretty tired by October.

Golf.title: Rules Guy: I hit my ball to the edge of the cup. How long can I wait for it to fall in?
Golf.summary: When your ball ends up on the edge of the cup, how long do you get to wait for it to fall in? Rules Guy has the answer. The post Rules Guy: I hit my ball to the edge of the cup. How long can I wait for it to fall in? appeared first on Golf .
Golf.copy:
The Rules of Golf are tricky! Thankfully, we’ve got the guru. Our Rules Guy knows the book front to back. Got a question? He’s got all the answers. Jack hits his approach to the very edge of the cup, while his playing partners all miss the putting surface. He checks on his ball but doesn’t mark it until the others are on the green, hoping it will fall in during the extended wait. Is this allowed? – Daryl Laumann, via email

By “very edge of the cup,” presumably you mean the ball is overhanging the edge. In this case, Jack gets a reasonable time to reach the ball, from however far away that might be, and then 10 seconds maximum to see if it will fall in — whether the other players have reached the green or not. (Clarification 13.3a/1 highlights the meaning of “reasonable time.”)

Golf.summary: LIV Golf captain withdraws from Hong Kong Open amid uncertain 2.0 future Golfmagic
bullets: Talor Gooch, captain of LIV Golf's OKGC, has withdrawn from this week's Hong Kong Open, an Asian Tour event, with no reason given. His withdrawal comes as players face a 25 October deadline, the final day of the tournament, to confirm whether they will take part in LIV 2.0, which is expected to be backed by BC Partners. Gooch has not said publicly whether he will stay.

LIV 2.0 would offer players equity but a reduced schedule of 10 tournaments and smaller purses, after the Saudi Public Investment Fund withdrew its investment this season. Jon Rahm, Adrian Meronk, Thomas Pieters and David Puig have said they will leave, while Sergio Garcia has terminated his contract and will return to the DP World Tour in 2027. The Hong Kong Open carries a $2 million prize fund, with the winner receiving invitations to the 2027 Masters and the 155th Open Championship at St Andrews.

Golf.title: Rory McIlroy reveals how LIV Golf’s rise put him and Tiger Woods at risk
Golf.summary: Rory McIlroy reveals how LIV Golf’s rise put him and Tiger Woods at risk Yahoo Sports
bullets: Rory McIlroy has said he and Tiger Woods were among the most vocal opponents of LIV Golf in 2022 partly because they had the most to lose in terms of stature within the PGA Tour. Speaking at the Bloomberg New Economy Forum in New Delhi on 13 October, he said LIV's emergence also affected TGL, their joint venture through TMRW Sports with the PGA Tour, whose rules generally require players to be PGA Tour members in good standing.

McIlroy said LIV wasted significant capital and could have used it more strategically, including by partnering with golf's governing bodies. He said he would now vote to allow former LIV golfers back onto the PGA Tour and DP World Tour, arguing their return could increase revenue and strengthen the tours' product. The DP World Tour has said players cannot compete on its circuit and in LIV 2.0 in 2027.
Golf.copy:
Rory McIlroy has explained why he and Tiger Woods became two of the strongest opponents of LIV Golf when the breakaway league emerged in 2022. Their resistance involved more than protecting the PGA Tour's established structure. McIlroy says both men had personal and professional interests that could suffer as golf fractured into competing circuits.

Their joint venture, TGL, was among the projects caught in that conflict. Now, as LIV faces bankruptcy proceedings and uncertainty over its future, McIlroy's latest comments offer fresh insight into the rivalry. His position has also softened as several LIV players reconsider their careers.

Golf.title: How a forgotten piece of NFL history pushed Roger Goodell's No. 2 to golf
Golf.summary: Roger Goodell's right-hand man surprised some when he left to take over a floundering PGA Tour. But his reasoning was even more surprising. The post How a forgotten piece of NFL history pushed Roger Goodell’s No. 2 to golf appeared first on Golf .
bullets: PGA Tour chief executive Brian Rolapp, formerly the long-time No. 2 to NFL commissioner Roger Goodell, said in a panel with The Athletic's Andrew Marchand that history drew him to the Tour. He had negotiated more than $100 billion in media rights deals at the NFL and was long seen as a candidate to succeed Goodell, who is 67.

Rolapp pointed to the AFL-NFL rivalry of the 1960s and baseball's CBA crisis as examples of chaos resetting a sport, saying the Tour is having its crisis later than others. In his first year he has driven changes including a split between "Championship" and "Challenger" series, the end of sponsor exemptions and a new championship format aimed at casual fans.
Golf.copy:
In the long and storied history of golf industry corporate hopscotch, few moves stand out like Brian Rolapp’s hire at the PGA Tour. Mostly because few moves have ever been so surprising.

The question looming over Rolapp’s arrival in golf wasn’t why the PGA Tour wanted Rolapp, the long-time No. 2 to NFL commissioner Roger Goodell. It was the opposite: Why did Rolapp want the PGA Tour?

Golf.title: 2 huge reasons golfers have early extension — and how to fix them
Golf.summary: GOLF Top 100 Teacher Brian Mogg explains two reasons he sees golfers early extend — and shares how to fix them. The post 2 huge reasons golfers have early extension — and how to fix them appeared first on Golf .
Golf.copy:
One of the most common swing problems I see among recreational golfers is early extension. You’ve probably heard the term before. It occurs when your hips and pelvis move toward the golf ball during the downswing, leaving less room for your arms and club to move freely through impact. The result? Your chest rises, your posture changes, and making consistent contact becomes much more difficult.

But here’s something I’ve learned after decades of teaching golfers around the world: Early extension is often the result of another swing flaw, not the original problem. That’s why simply telling a golfer to keep their hips back doesn’t always work. To make a lasting improvement, you need to understand what’s causing your hips to move toward the ball in the first place.
